subject: On-prem VPC hardware fabric: failover scenarios & control-plane boundary
messages:
From: Samantha Lee <samantha@acme-analytics.com>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Cc: acme-netops@acme-analytics.com
Date: 2026-10-11T08:14:00-07:00
Subject: On-prem VPC hardware fabric: failover scenarios and SLA questions

Hi Jonas / Laura —

Thanks again for taking this on. We're finalizing the on-prem spec for the private VPC deployment and want to validate the hardware fabric failover modes and control-plane boundary assumptions before we lock in rack/cabling. Key items from our side:

- Two data-center sites (primary / secondary) with Layer 3 BGP between them; they want to avoid asymmetric return routing during failover.
- OOB management network for control-plane (separate VLAN preferred).
- Firewalls are stateful and will NAT egress; we need expected ports/flows and suggested source IPs for allowlists.
- SLA ask: if local infra loses connectivity for >5 min, can Redwood offer a documented fallback (graceful degrade to hosted model or partial read-only mode)?

Attached is our Deploy Requirements doc and a preliminary fabric diagram. Can you review failover scenarios (link/stateful NAT behavior) and confirm whether Redwood's control-plane agents need inbound reachability or only outbound? Also would like recommended healthcheck endpoints and expected connection counts for a 10k qps peak.

Keen to close this this week so procurement can finalize hardware.

Samantha
NetOps Lead — Acme Analytics

Attachments: acme-deploy-requirements.pdf (pdf)

From: jonas_weber@redwood.com
To: Samantha Lee <samantha@acme-analytics.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: 2026-10-11T10:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: On-prem VPC hardware fabric: failover scenarios and SLA questions

Hi Samantha — thanks for the detail and the diagram. High level answers first, then a short action checklist below.

Summary answers:
- Control plane behavior: Redwood's private deployment uses outbound-only connections from the control-plane hosts to the customer-managed control plane endpoint (port 443 TLS). No inbound holes required by default. We do, however, recommend an OOB management network for tenant/ops access and for HA heartbeats between control-plane nodes.
- Failover modes: For the data-plane, we support active-active with per-request affinity or active-passive based on your LB choice. With BGP between DCs, recommend symmetric routing (same egress path) for stable KV cache behavior.
- SLA fallback: We support a pre-configured fallback to Redwood-hosted inference endpoints for critical routes. That requires a mutually-agreed policy (data-tagging for PII), and a signed POA so we can enable cross-account routing.

Quick checklist / action items:
1) Please confirm whether the management OOB VLAN can reach our management CIDR outbound (we'll provide exact IPs).
2) Confirm BGP failover behavior: do you prefer active-active eBGP with equal-cost or active-passive with prepull? This impacts KV cache warming.
3) Approve a short list of allowed outbound ports (we recommend: 443, 2200 for ssh management, 123 for NTP).
4) Provide expected peak concurrency per node (10k qps overall — we estimate ~2500 connections per inference pod under average prompt length).

I've sketched a fabric diagram with suggested control-plane demarcation and HA proxy placement — see attached vpc-fabric-draft.drawio and the folder link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2B3cVpcDiagram

If helpful, we can do a 30-min netops walk-through later today.

— Jonas
Sr. Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Attachment: vpc-fabric-draft.drawio (drawio)

From: laura_bennett@redwood.com
To: jonas_weber@redwood.com, Samantha Lee <samantha@acme-analytics.com>
Cc: markus_klein@redwood.com
Date: 2026-10-11T13:27:00-07:00
Subject: Re: On-prem VPC hardware fabric: failover scenarios and SLA questions

Thanks — a couple of control-plane specifics from my side:

- Control-plane network: we strongly prefer that control-plane nodes sit on a dedicated management VLAN with egress-only access to Redwood's control endpoint. That keeps the data-plane demarcation clean and simplifies audit logging.
- Egress IPs: I will provide a stable set of egress IPs (we rotate quarterly) — for the initial rollout please allow the block listed in the attached CSV.
- KMS/HSM: If you plan to host keys on-prem, we need an HSM reachable from the control-plane for envelope operations. If not, we can integrate your cloud KMS via a site-to-site encrypted tunnel.
- Healthchecks: recommended endpoints: /health/live (1s), /health/ready (3s), and a tokenized /metrics/ping for load balancer decisions. TCP healthchecks are insufficient for the control-plane because KV sync state matters.

I added a simple control-plane egress table in the attachment for your firewall team to import. Also recommend putting a stateful HAProxy in front of inference workers with a short session timeout to allow for quick failback.

-Laura
Director, Private Deployments | Redwood Inference

Attachment: controlplane-egress-table.csv (csv)

From: Samantha Lee <samantha@acme-analytics.com>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.com, jonas_weber@redwood.com

Subject: Re: On-prem VPC hardware fabric: failover scenarios and SLA questions

Laura / Jonas —

This is helpful. A few follow-ups from our procurement and netops teams:

- Procurement: need written confirmation that Redwood's fallback to hosted endpoints will not retain raw customer requests in Cleartext and that any routed data will be tagged and isolated per contract. Can you supply a short statement we can attach to the PO?
- NetOps: our ops lead asked whether the HAProxy layer can be configured for health-based draining and whether Greenwood (our LB vendor) will play nicely with session affinity for long-running streaming calls.

We can provision OOB VLAN connectivity next week. We'd also like a short runbook for an outage scenario (primary DC network failure) that lists exact steps for failing traffic, expected RTO, and manual cutover commands. Do you have an operational playbook we can adapt?

Samantha

Samantha —

Short answers to your follow-ups and next steps:

1) PO statement for procurement: "Redwood Inference confirms that if an agreed fallback to Redwood-hosted inference is enacted, customer request payloads will be tagged, encrypted in transit, and processed in a dedicated tenant space. Redwood will not persist raw request content beyond the duration necessary for inference unless explicitly authorized in the contract." (Please note: procurement should attach this to the PO — legal is happy to provide a signed addendum if needed.)

2) HAProxy & session affinity: Yes — configure the HAProxy layer with health-based draining (graceful shutdown) and a consistent-hash persistence for affinity. For long streaming calls, we recommend heartbeat keepalive and connection tracking TTL >= 120s. Greenwood LB vendors typically support this; we'll coordinate a validation test during cutover.

3) Runbook: I've drafted an outage playbook (preflight checks, cutover commands, and verification steps). It's a short doc we can share and edit together: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2B3cVpcDiagram (folder contains: runbooks/onprem-outage-playbook.md). Expected RTO for automatic failover (BGP convergence + LB drain) is ~90–180s depending on your eBGP timers; manual failover procedures reduce risk for cache inconsistency and have an expected RTO of ~5–10 min.

Next steps:
- I'll upload the runbook draft to the Drive and create a shared edit session.
- Can we lock a 30-min validation with your NetOps on Tue 2026-10-13 09:00 PT?
- I'll get legal to draft the signed addendum for the PO fallback clause.

If that works, I'll move the diagram into a final version and send the appliance IP list next.

— Jonas
Sr. Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
